source.title: How Does Batch Normalization Help Binary Training
source.authors: Eyyub Sari; Mouloud Belbahri; V. Nia

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports CIFAR-10 experiments varying initialization and BatchNorm components in binary networks, with accuracy outcomes bearing on the broader training claim but not measuring the behaviors specified by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports best Top1 accuracy across initialization settings and maximum accuracy after BatchNorm component ablations. It does not report training classification error, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, or trainable depth. Its rows therefore do not directly measure the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization sensitivity and BatchNorm component effects on final accuracy and convergence in binary networks. It does not measure initialization effects on learning speed or trainable depth (V4), or BatchNorm effects on accuracy gain speed or learning-rate tolerance (V6). Its theoretical gradient-variance analysis does not establish those outcomes. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they argue that BatchNorm prevents gradient explosion in binary networks, that conventional full-precision initialization variance prescriptions are unnecessary there, and that centering with suitable fixed scaling can replace BatchNorm. BatchNorm is therefore not indispensable as a layer. The theoretical scale reaches 79.6%, while an adjusted scale reaches 87.9% against BatchNorm's 88.8%.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains binary quantized CIFAR-10 networks with Adam and cross-entropy, varying initialization variance and BatchNorm components; it does not use the claim versions' full-precision network recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization variance has little reported effect on VGG and ResNet-56 accuracy; MobileNet-v1 is more sensitive. For binarized ResNet-56, removing scaling or BatchNorm substantially reduces reported accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG best Top1 accuracy ranges from 90.4% to 90.7% across the tested initializations, versus 90.5% with Glorot initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested binary VGG's final accuracy is relatively insensitive to symmetric initialization variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary ResNet-56 reaches 88.8% with BatchNorm, 79.6% with centering and theoretical scaling, and 31.7% with either centering alone or no BatchNorm. Adjusted scaling reaches 87.9%, a condition omitted from the rows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this binary ResNet-56 recipe, appropriate fixed scaling with centering can substantially recover BatchNorm accuracy; removing scaling produces nonconvergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 additionally reports ResNet-56 accuracies of 86.9–88.8% versus 88.5% with Glorot, and MobileNet-v1 accuracies of 68.9–73.2% versus 71.7% with Glorot.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity of binary-network final accuracy to initialization variance depends on architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 derives exploding gradient variance without BatchNorm and approximate stabilization with BatchNorm under initialization assumptions and suitable layer-width ratios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm can control gradient-variance growth at initialization in binary networks under the theorem's assumptions.

record.problems: Experiments are limited to CIFAR-10. Numerical outcomes are accuracy values rather than training classification error; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The authors note their initialization assumptions become inaccurate as training proceeds.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including fitting corrupted or random labels, and its dependence on model size or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity-shortcut prevention, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain-network training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
BatchNorm effects on accuracy gain speed and tolerance to higher learning rates; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The source is internally consistent on the Table 2 mapping when its prose is consulted: both No Scale and No BN reach 31.7%. The record omitted the adjusted-scaling condition and shifted two condition-value assignments. Missing related endpoints are described under fits_no_version; none warrants a missing entry for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments use binary networks and report accuracy, not training classification error or corrupted/random-label fitting.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU experiment or width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual shortcut comparison or depth sweep.
The study varies initialization variance in binary networks but does not measure training speed or trainable depth, nor compare the initialization methods and settings named in this version.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss trajectory, sharpness measurement, or divergence comparison.

The study compares final accuracy for binary networks with BatchNorm, fixed scaling, centering only, and no BatchNorm. It does not measure speed of accuracy gain or tolerance to higher learning rates, nor test Fixup.
